articles.author: Matthew Gault
articles.summary: Some people spent the week leading up to the release of Grand Theft Auto VI replaying the old games. I, sicko that I am, spent it watching TV news coverage of the franchise from the past 20 years. Grand Theft Auto has been a staple of cable and broadcast TV news since at least the release of Grand Theft Auto III in 2001. I’ve been an adult for all of it; I’ve had a front row seat for two decades of moral panics, parental freakouts, and bizarre political theater. The games and the broader culture’s reaction to them have changed dramatically in that time. In 2001, newscasters worried GTA III was training an army of young men to kill. In 2026, The New York Times earnestly quoted Bell Hooks in its review of GTA VI. For mainstream news, GTA is the ur-video game. The Trump DOJ argued that blocking the results was necessary to prevent "voter confusion" caused by the presence of two candidates with very similar names on the ballot. As I explained previously , Republican candidate Dan J. Sullivan can potentially be confused with Dan S. Sullivan (the incumbent GOP senator), and some voters might have accidentally chosen Dan J. even though they intended to back Dan S. Today, as reported by prominent election law scholar Rick Hasen, DOJ filed a brief in the US Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit seeking to dismiss the case. They also want the district court ruling vacated for procedural reasons (I will not opine on whether that's warranted).
